items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: If you take Charlie Parker, who I haven’t heard anybody in jazz surpass that.

ctx.x: You preceded one of my questions which I think is terrific, and the thought process and how much jazz pedagogy can be in your head now, and how much it actually helps. So a big part of your life has been teaching. Is part of what you think your task is is to make things as simple for your students as possible?

Well actually if you — it’s a perception. If you can perceive the simplicity, that’s where it’s at. If you take Charlie Parker, who I haven’t heard anybody in jazz surpass that. If you break down each little fragment of his stuff it’s something simple, but the way he puts that all together is profound. You know. And I tell my students, “Can you play a B major scale?” [Nods head] “Can you play a G major scale?” [Nods yes] “Can you play E flat major scale?” Um hum. I say then you can play “Giant Steps” because…
How do you have them work on that? To get more rhythm in their playing?
